look_here_first: Look for the small spurred yellow flowers, then check for erect, often straight capsules and inconspicuous self-pollinating (cleistogamous) flower clusters. Measure mature seeds and inspect the margin; do not rely on raceme height or capsule length alone because subspecies vary.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Approved Master Plant Pool source; native-range confirmation in three project target counties not established.

morphology_keys.habit: Glaucous to green, branched winter annual, often 20–40 cm with multiple erect or ascending stems.
morphology_keys.leaves: Finely divided alternate leaves, ultimate lobes ovate to obovate, sometimes with minute abrupt tips.
morphology_keys.flowers: Bilateral yellow flowers in terminal and lateral racemes; four petals, one spurred; spurred outer petal usually 11–15 mm, spur 4–7 mm. Some racemes bear minute cleistogamous flowers.
morphology_keys.fruits: Mostly erect linear capsules, often about 10–35 mm across the species and subspecies; shiny seeds around 1.5 mm diameter lacking a marginal ring in the FNA treatment.
best_field_traits: Photograph the side-view flower and rearward spur
Check mature capsule angle and shape
Use seed margin and size under magnification; assess subspecies variability

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. micrantha commonly has smaller flowers, relatively erect capsules, smaller ringless seeds and sometimes inconspicuous cleistogamous flowers; C. aurea often has larger flowers and may have spreading or hanging curved capsules. Fruit and raceme lengths overlap, especially with southern subspecies; require multiple characters.
comparisons.cautions: Do not assume every C. micrantha has short racemes or 10–15 mm fruits: subsp. australis and texensis may have longer racemes and fruits. Subspecies identification needs its own key; source-pool Corydalis curvisiliqua subsp. curvisiliqua remains an unresolved/reference concept, not duplicated.
